description: From the pedestrian esplanade on Calle Alcazabilla, the 1st-century Roman theatre glows softly under the street lamps, its curved limestone cavea centered in the frame. The Alcazaba's Moorish walls rise dark and massive directly behind the ancient stones, with the lit city shimmering beyond. It is a clear, mild Málaga night — about 21°C with barely a breeze — and the empty plaza gives the ruins a quiet, almost private feeling.

prompts.prompt-r1.txt: Photorealistic original artistic interpretation (not a photograph) of the Roman Theatre of Malaga, Spain, at night. Tourist viewpoint: the Calle Alcazabilla esplanade at street level, looking up at the semicircular stone cavea with the Alcazaba fortress walls rising directly behind it. Frame: the ancient Roman stone seating (cavea) centered, weathered limestone tiers curving in a semicircle; the Alcazaba's Moorish walls and towers looming dark above and behind the theatre; the modern glass interpretation centre at the theatre's edge and the empty esplanade in the foreground. Night light: warm glow from the esplanade street lamps washing the lower stonework, the fortress a dark silhouette with faint city lights beyond, clear moonlit sky, 21 degrees C, light breeze. Main subject centered to survive a 4:5 center crop. No identifiable people, no legible logos, no text, lettering or signs anywhere in the image. Keep the lower third clean and uncluttered.
